extraction.condition: persons or class of persons who opt for dispute resolution under this Chapter and fulfil specified conditions
extraction.action: The Dispute Resolution Committee may make modifications to the variations in specified order.
extraction.consequence: Grant immunity from prosecution for any offence punishable under this Act, or modify penalties imposed by assessment orders.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where the Central Government's creation of Dispute Resolution Committees enables these bodies to modify assessment orders and penalties for eligible individuals who opt into dispute resolution under specified conditions.

extraction.condition: being assessed as representative assessee
extraction.action: liability to assessment and proceedings under this Act in his own name only; tax levied upon him similarly to the person represented by him.
extraction.consequence: Directly being assessed or having tax payable on chargeable part of trust income, regardless of Chapter provisions
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where the role of 'representative assessee' triggers specific assessment and tax recovery actions as outlined in points (a) to (c).

extraction.condition: recognition is accorded to a provident fund with existing balances
extraction.action: an account must be made showing each employee's balance and further particulars as prescribed.
extraction.consequence: Balance not transferred shall incur income-tax liability, except for the recognised part of the funds which will show a credited 'transferred balance'.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text outlines actions and consequences directly following the recognition of a provident fund's balance; it mandates account creation with specific details for tax purposes.

extraction.condition: The last figure in an amount is five or more
extraction.action: Increase such amount to the next higher multiple of ten.
extraction.consequence: Determines total income for tax assessment purposes under this Act.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text outlines a specific rule where an amount is adjusted based on the last digit being five or more, directly affecting tax assessment calculations for individuals.

extraction.condition: the payment of tax payable by the company or making any such priority-payment secured creditors; meeting costs related to winding up
extraction.action: liquidator' extraneous actions as per subsections (1), (3) and parts with assets in contravention must be avoided.
extraction.consequence: personal liability for the company tax payment by liquidator if conditions are not met or proper notice is not given
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where the liquidator's failure to adhere to specific actions regarding tax payments or priority secured creditor debts leads directly to personal liability for those amounts.

extraction.condition: every person domiciled in India at the time of his departure
extraction.action: shall furnish, in prescribed form to income-tax authority or such other authority as prescribed: PAN allotted under section 262; purpose of visit outside India; estimated period of stay outside India.
actors: every person domiciled in India at the time of his departure
extraction.reasoning: The legal text outlines a causal policy rule where individuals domiciled in India must provide specific information to tax authorities before leaving for an overseas visit.

extraction.condition: the repealed Income-tax Act shall continue to apply
extraction.action: carry out proceedings as per the procedure specified in the repealed Income-tax Act
extraction.consequence: any penalty may be imposed under the provisions of the repealed act for tax years beginning before April 1, 2026
thresholds: April 1, 2026
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where the repealed Income-tax Act's provisions continue to govern proceedings for tax years before April 1, 2026 and penalties can be imposed as if this new act had not been enacted.

extraction.condition: The assessee has been previously assessed for total income of any tax year by regular assessment.
extraction.action: Require person to pay advance tax on specified sum as per the order in writing issued by Assessing Officer.
extraction.consequence: Payment must be made following an order, with subsequent notices under section 289 if necessary.
thresholds: Total income of the latest tax year assessed by regular assessment or total income returned for any return furnished in a subsequent tax year.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes that if an individual has undergthy been regularly assessed and deemed liable to pay advance tax by the Assessing Officer based on their income assessment or returns furnished for subsequent years.

extraction.condition: the service of a worker has been interrupted by the transfer
extraction.action: compensation shall be deemed received at time of transfer.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where the transfer of an undertaking'dictates that compensation is due to affected workers if their service interruption conditions are met.

extraction.condition: The deduction of tax should not occur from any payment made for services under an agreement wherein the payer bears the tax charge.
extraction.action: Increase income to a net amount payable as per such agreements before applying tax provisions
extraction.consequence: Ensuring that after-tax amounts match what is due according to specific arrangements, without direct deduction at source from pension system trusts.
actors: person liable to pay income or sum
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal link where tax deductions are not applied directly from pension system trusts and instead requires adjustments to income before applying standard provisions.

extraction.condition: the applicant is a registered non-profit organisation and has adopted or undertaken modification of its objects within thirty days after the adoption date
extraction.action: submit an application for registration/modification as per legal requirements
extraction.consequence: if not submitted in time, may be condoned by Principal Commissioner or Commissioner with reasonable cause; otherwise provisions apply based on income over five crore rupees during preceding two tax years if the total exceeds ten crore for a decade-long period as per amended regulations
thresholds: 30 days after adoption/modification of objects, six months from the end of quarter when application is made, five tax years commencing with the start year
five crore rupees income threshold for specific provisions to apply; ten-year period as an alternative
extraction.reasoning: The legal text outlines a causal relationship wherein non-profit organisations must submit applications within specified timeframes following object adoption/modification and income thresholds for certain provisions to apply.

extraction.condition: an offence under this Act has been committed by a Hindu undivided family
extraction.action: the karta thereof shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
extraction.consequence: punishment as per law for committing an offence under this Act.
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal policy rule where the karta of a Hindu Undivided Family is held responsible for offences committed by them unless they can prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

extraction.condition: an order has been made in favour of any person
extraction.action: he shall not be entitled to any relief under this section at any time after the making of such an order.
thresholds: one lakh rupees
extraction.reasoning: The legal text establishes a causal policy rule where the making of an order disqualifies the assessee from seeking relief for any other tax year.
